citation: Sheahan, James W., and George P. Upton. The Great Conflagration. Chicago: Its Past, Present and Future. Philadelphia: Union Publishing Co., 1871.
author: James W. Sheahan and George P. Upton
repository: Internet Archive, from the Cornell University Library copy
locator: Title page (scan leaf 7: 'By James W. Sheahan and George P. Upton'); the count of the burnt wards from the census of 1871, scan leaf 57: 'Rendered homeless, 98,860'.
rights_note: Published 1871 in the United States; public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-16 (T-2611) through the Internet Archive's full-text search of this scan, at the leaves the locator names; the page images were not opened.
note: Two Chicago newspapermen writing within weeks of the fire, so period evidence. Its figure of 98,860 people made homeless is its own computation, ward by ward from the census of 1871; other accounts printed in the same book give larger round numbers, so the caption says about 100,000. Used for one time-stream caption on the way to 1812 and 1835 (the year 1871); nothing in any scene is built from it.
what_it_supplies: the authors' count of the people made homeless by the fire of October 1871: 98,860
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about the buildings of 1812 or 1835: the town those scenes show was gone long before 1871
